texts: good. parses as a non-factive report: Brindle Coombe as the one saying it, the Council as the place, day 96 of Year 1 on the saying, and the whole 'behind on mire-essence' claim sealed under the report rather than asserted as fact.
good. same shape as the first sentence, with the village and the Council carried over as the same symbols, so the two reported shortfalls hang off one speaker and one meeting.

good. the sealed complement keeps 'would' as future-relative-to-the-saying, and the forcing and the dimming come out as two linked events with the village named only as the one that would dim the lanterns — which is what the sentence says.

good. 'keeps the Stilllight Lantern lit' gets the maintenance shape (a lit state held in continuation, plus the plain 'the lantern is lit' fact), and 'always' coincides with the full strength the sealed atoms already carry, so nothing is lost by its having no separate carrier of its own.
